learn.hook: Your morning milk, the bus to school, the light in your classroom and the water in the tap all depend on something invisible: infrastructure!
points: Infrastructure means the basic facilities and services a country needs to work and grow, like roads, railways, ports, airports, electricity, water supply, telephones and the internet.
Physical infrastructure includes transport, energy, water and communication networks. Social infrastructure includes schools, hospitals and other services for people.
Good infrastructure helps farmers sell crops, factories get raw materials, children reach school and patients reach hospitals. That is why it is called an engine of development.

Many infrastructure facilities are public goods: once provided, they can be used by everyone, and one person's use does not stop another's. Street lights, lighthouses and national defence are examples.
Because private companies may not earn profits from public goods, governments usually build and pay for them using tax money.

example.q: A village gets a new all-weather road to the town. List two ways this can change villagers' lives.
steps: Farmers can take vegetables and milk to the town market quickly and get better prices.
Children can reach a school and patients can reach a hospital even in the rainy season.
Buses and shops may come to the village, creating jobs.
example.answer: Any two: better prices for farm goods, easier access to schools and hospitals, more transport and jobs.

learn.reallife: A street light outside your home lights the road for everyone who walks by; that's a public good in action.

games.title: Public goods: true or false?
items: A street light is a public good.
Everyone on the road benefits, and one person's use does not reduce another's.
Public goods are usually provided by the government.
They are often paid for with taxes.
A chocolate bar you buy is a public good.
Only the buyer can eat it; it is a private good.
It supports farming, industry, health and education.
Lighthouses guide all ships that pass by.
A lighthouse helps every ship, which is why it is a public good.

quiz.q: What is infrastructure?
options: Basic facilities like roads, power and water that a country needs
quiz.explain: Infrastructure is the network of basic facilities that support all economic and social activity.
quiz.mistake: Thinks infrastructure means only buildings

quiz.q: Which is an example of social infrastructure?
quiz.explain: Schools and hospitals serve people's health and education: social infrastructure.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up physical and social infrastructure

quiz.q: Which of these is a public good?
options: A bag of rice you bought
quiz.explain: A street light benefits everyone, and one person's use does not stop another's.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything useful is a public good

quiz.q: Why do governments usually provide public goods?
options: Public goods are always free to make
Private companies may not make profits from them, but everyone needs them
quiz.explain: Since people cannot easily be charged for them, the government uses taxes to provide them.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand why markets may not supply public goods

quiz.q: Why is infrastructure called an 'engine of development'?
options: It powers growth in farming, industry, health and education
It is a real engine on trains
quiz.explain: Roads, power and communication let every other activity grow.
quiz.mistake: Takes the phrase literally

quiz.q: How does an all-weather road help a farmer?
options: It makes the crops grow taller
She can take crops to market quickly and get better prices
quiz.explain: Faster, reliable transport helps farmers sell fresh produce.
quiz.mistake: Does not link transport with farmers' income

quiz.q: Which is NOT physical infrastructure?
quiz.explain: Teachers serve education (social); the others are physical facilities.
quiz.mistake: Confuses services by people with physical networks

quiz.q: Who usually pays for public infrastructure like roads and bridges?
quiz.explain: Taxes paid by citizens fund much of India's infrastructure.
quiz.mistake: Does not link taxes with public services

teach.ask: Gappu asks what infrastructure means and why it matters. Explain it to him.
teach.praise: Roads, power, water, schools and hospitals: the engine that runs the country. I see it everywhere now!
teach.nudge: Good! Can you also tell me what a public good is?

learn.hook: On 16 April 1853, India's first passenger train puffed 34 km from Bori Bunder in Mumbai to Thane. Today trains carry crores of passengers!
points: India has one of the largest road networks in the world: National Highways, State Highways, district roads and village roads. The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (2000) connects villages with all-weather roads.
The Golden Quadrilateral highway links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata. The North–South corridor links Srinagar and Kanyakumari, and the East–West corridor links Silchar and Porbandar.

Indian Railways' first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 between Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane. The Chenab Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir is the world's highest railway arch bridge. India's first metro railway opened in Kolkata in 1984.
Air transport is the fastest way to travel long distances. The UDAN scheme aims to make flights affordable and connect smaller towns.
Most of India's foreign trade by volume travels by sea through ports like Mumbai, Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Navi Mumbai), Chennai, Kolkata, Visakhapatnam, Kochi and Paradip.

example.q: A train leaves Bori Bunder and travels the same 34 km route to Thane as the first train. If it covers 17 km in the first half hour at the same speed, how long will the whole trip take?
steps: So it takes 2 × half an hour = 1 hour.

learn.reallife: When your family books a train or flight on an app, or orders something shipped from another city, you are using India's transport infrastructure.

games.title: Transport facts
pairs: Links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata

games.title: India's transport milestones
items: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana begins (2000)

quiz.q: On which date did India's first passenger train run?
quiz.explain: It ran from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane on 16 April 1853.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous dates

quiz.q: How long was the route of India's first passenger train?
quiz.explain: The Bori Bunder–Thane route was about 34 km.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a much longer distance

quiz.q: The Golden Quadrilateral links which four cities?
quiz.explain: It connects the four big metro cities in a rough square.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with the corridors

quiz.q: The North–South corridor links Srinagar with:
quiz.explain: It runs from Srinagar in the north to Kanyakumari in the south.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two corridors

quiz.q: Where did India's first metro railway open, in 1984?
quiz.explain: Kolkata Metro opened in 1984; Delhi Metro came later.
quiz.mistake: Assumes Delhi had the first metro

quiz.q: Which scheme connects villages with all-weather roads?
quiz.explain: PMGSY, started in 2000, builds rural roads.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up government schemes

quiz.q: What is the aim of the UDAN scheme?
options: To make flights affordable and connect smaller towns
quiz.explain: UDAN focuses on regional air connectivity.
quiz.mistake: Confuses air and road schemes

quiz.q: The Chenab Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir is famous as the world's:
quiz.explain: It is the highest railway arch bridge in the world.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what makes the bridge special

teach.ask: Gappu flies everywhere, but humans need transport! Tell him about India's roads, railways, airways and ports.
teach.praise: Highways, trains, planes and ships carry people and goods all over India. What a network!
teach.nudge: Good! Which transport carries most of India's foreign trade, and when did the first train run?

topics.title: Power, communication and our shared responsibility

learn.hook: A tiny phone in a village can now make a video call to a doctor in a big city. Power lines and internet cables make it possible!
points: Electricity comes from many sources: thermal power (from coal or gas), hydroelectric power (from flowing water), nuclear power, and renewable sources like solar and wind energy.
Renewable energy, especially solar and wind, is growing quickly in India because it does not run out and causes less pollution. Rajasthan and Gujarat have large solar parks.

Communication infrastructure includes India Post, telephones, mobile networks and the internet. The six-digit PIN code system was introduced in 1972. BharatNet aims to bring broadband internet to every gram panchayat.
Good internet lets people use online banking, learning, health services and government services from home.
Infrastructure is a shared responsibility. Citizens should not damage public property, waste electricity or water, or litter on roads and trains, because repairs cost public money.

example.q: A family switches off fans and lights when leaving a room. How does this small act help the whole country?
steps: Less coal needs to be burnt in thermal plants, so there is less pollution.
More power is available for homes, hospitals and factories.
example.answer: It saves electricity, reduces pollution and leaves more power for others.

learn.reallife: Look at your electricity bill or a solar panel on a rooftop; these show how energy infrastructure reaches your home.

items.text: Electricity from flowing water is called ___ power.
BharatNet aims to bring ___ to every gram panchayat.

quiz.q: Electricity produced from flowing water is called:
quiz.explain: 'Hydro' means water; dams use flowing water to turn turbines.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up energy sources

quiz.q: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
quiz.explain: Sunlight does not run out, so solar energy is renewable.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all energy sources are the same

quiz.q: Why is solar energy good for the environment?
options: It causes less pollution and does not run out
quiz.explain: Solar panels make electricity from sunlight without burning fuel.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the benefit of renewables

quiz.q: How many digits does an Indian PIN code have?
quiz.explain: The PIN code, introduced in 1972, has six digits.
quiz.mistake: Guesses the length

quiz.q: What is BharatNet's aim?
options: To bring broadband internet to every gram panchayat
quiz.explain: BharatNet is laying optical fibre to connect villages to the internet.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up infrastructure projects

quiz.q: Which is an example of communication infrastructure?
quiz.explain: Mobile towers carry phone and internet signals.
quiz.mistake: Confuses natural features with built infrastructure

quiz.q: Why should citizens not damage public property like trains and bus stops?
options: It is fun to break things
Public property belongs to no one
Repairs cost public money that could be used for other services
quiz.explain: Public property is paid for with taxes; damage wastes everyone's money.
quiz.mistake: Thinks public property belongs to no one

quiz.q: How does good internet help people in villages?
options: It makes their crops grow faster
They can use online learning, banking and health services
quiz.explain: Internet connects villages to services that were once only in cities.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how communication helps development

teach.ask: Gappu wonders where electricity and the internet come from, and how he can help. Explain to him.
teach.praise: Power from sun, wind, water and coal, internet everywhere, and we must all take care of it. I'll switch off the lights!
teach.nudge: Good! How can people like us help take care of infrastructure?
